title: PRD: Operationalize incident-derived throttling windows and tenant degradation budgets
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Translate postmortem actions from a recent multi-tenant tail-latency incident into concrete PRD requirements: define throttling windows, tenant-level degradation budgets, and rollout/verification criteria so the runtime can automatically protect system SLOs while minimizing customer disruption.
background: A Jan incident identified that sudden KV-cache stalls and a burst of long-sequence requests caused sustained tail latency for a subset of tenants. Postmortem recommended bounded tenant throttles, a tenant degradation budget model, and synthetic verification to prevent regressions. This PRD captures product requirements to operationalize those recommendations into the serving runtime and Console UX.
scope: Requirements and acceptance criteria for: (1) tenant-level degradation budgets (daily/hourly), (2) automatic throttling windows and backoff policies that can be applied per-tenant and per-route, (3) Console controls for operators to view and adjust budgets and throttles, (4) synthetic tests and runbook hooks to verify behavior during rollout.
out_of_scope: Changes to core kernel scheduling algorithms, model quantization logic, or billing adjustments; these will be handled in separate engineering initiatives.
acceptance_criteria: Engine exposes per-tenant degradation_budget config with hourly and daily tokens and a documented rate of consumption
Runtime enforces throttling windows when a tenant consumes >90% of its hourly budget: min-latency-preserving throttles applied and documented fallbacks triggered
Console UI shows live budget consumption, projected burn rate, and a one-click temporary increase/decrease control for on-call
Automated synthetic traffic test verifies throttling behavior under burst sequences and fails CI if throttling is not applied per policy
Standard runbook steps created: alert->investigate->apply-temporary-adjustment->escalate; linked to PagerDuty and incident timeline templates
tradeoffs: Aggressive throttling reduces system-wide tail latency but increases likelihood of customer errors or degraded UX
Conservative budgets minimize customer disruption but risk SLO breaches for other tenants during noisy neighbors
Exposing controls in Console favors operator flexibility but increases surface area for misconfiguration
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flag behind 'tenant-degradation-budgets' in staging with synthetic tests (1 week)
Phase 1: Canary to 5% of traffic (non-critical tenants) with monitoring dashboards and auto-rollback on SLO regressions (2 weeks)
Phase 2: Gradual ramp to 100% for new tenant cohorts and opt-in for existing tenants; provide self-serve UI for budget tuning (3 weeks)
Phase 3: Default enforcement for all tenants with operator guardrails and documented runbooks (2 weeks)
